name: IRC_PURGE_HISTORY
description: The table is use to store history of recruiting purging job execution information for each entity

columns.name: PURGE_HISTORY_ID
columns.description: Primary key of the table. System generated

columns.name: ESS_REQUEST_ID
columns.description: The process id of the ESS job that purged the entity

columns.name: ENTITY_ID
columns.description: This stores entity name that was purged.

columns.name: ACTIVE_DAYS
columns.description: Number of active days kept in the entity.

columns.name: BATCH_SIZE
columns.description: The number of rows to be purged in each batch for each entity type.

columns.name: EXECUTION_ORDER
columns.description: The priority order of the entity that was purged.

columns.name: ENTITIES_PURGED_COUNT
columns.description: The number of entities that were purged.

columns.name: START_TIME
columns.description: Start time of the purge process for a entity.

columns.name: END_TIME
columns.description: End time of the purge process for a entity.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: This stores the status of the purge process e.g. IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELED, FAILED etc.

columns.name: ERROR_CODE
columns.description: This is use to store error codes, which could be oracle error code or custom error codes.

columns.name: ERROR_MESSAGE
columns.description: The error message returned by PL/SQL. This could be both oracle error message and custom error message.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.
